WF-03 Step 4 (regression test) for ISS-0119. Build the two test files the design specifies and PERFORM the fail-first demonstration. §7 gives assertions A0-A8, §7.1 gives the required procedure and the four outputs you must quote, §8 gives the digest definition.

CREATE: test/support/status_history.ex (module Letflow.Test.StatusHistory, six functions plus current_volume/2 and default_ceilings/0, signatures in §7), test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs (assertions A0-A8), test/specs/ISS-0119.md (the test spec, carrying the fail-first evidence). ELIXIR-DEV deliberately did NOT create the two test files -- they are yours. mix.exs:20 already puts test/support on the :test load path, verified independently by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and REVIEWER at both HEAD and the pre-fix commit, so no build-config change is needed.

=== THREE CONDITIONS CARRIED FROM REVIEWER'S STEP 3D RULING, all binding ===

C1 -- APPLY THE §8 ERRATUM AND USE THE CORRECTED FORM. ELIXIR-DEV found, and REVIEWER independently reproduced, that §8's THREE digest implementations do not agree as §8 claims. Bash normative and PowerShell both yield 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804 (355,610 bytes hashed). §8's ELIXIR form as written yields 5c9fda42d72b0d46e4bf60cfc5a0fc044d7c36eb0192bc4b5e599c2a559b657a (361,376 bytes) -- exactly +5,766, one byte per line. Cause: File.stream!/1 opens in TEXT MODE on a CRLF checkout and has already stripped the CR, so String.trim_trailing(&1, "\r\n") -- which trims only that exact two-byte suffix -- matches nothing, the surviving \n stays, and <> "\n" appends a second. REVIEWER confirmed the mechanism directly: File.stream! yields line 1 as "# RoCo — Requirement run history\n", a bare \n. USE THIS CORRECTED FORM, which REVIEWER verified reproduces the normative value:

  File.stream!(path) |> Enum.take(n) |> Enum.map_join("", &((&1 |> String.trim_trailing("\n") |> String.trim_trailing("\r")) <> "\n")) |> then(&:crypto.hash(:sha256, &1)) |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: trim "\n" FIRST, then "\r"; never the literal two-byte "\r\n". This is what makes it correct on both a CRLF text-mode read and an LF/binary read, i.e. portable to CI where the checkout is LF. Quote the digest your test ACTUALLY computes and state whether it equals 5a1a64ab...804 -- §8's CHECK 5 was never dischargeable at Step 3 because the test did not exist yet, and ELIXIR-DEV correctly said so rather than claiming it.

C2 -- CORRECT §8 INLINE, in the same commit, marked as an erratum ruled at Step 3d. REVIEWER's reason is exactly this run's own subject matter: an erratum that lives only in a handoff is the 'recorded where nobody lands' failure ISS-0119 is about. You are explicitly authorized to edit lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md for THIS ONE CORRECTION ONLY -- §8's Elixir bullet and any sentence claiming the three forms agree. Change nothing else in the artefact; it passed a hard gate on its third pass and the rest of it is not yours to revise.

C3 -- ONE ExUnit `test` BLOCK PER ASSERTION. A0 through A8 each get their own block. This is not style: ExUnit aborts a block at its first failed assertion, and A0 is EXPECTED to fail in the pre-fix run (no index exists there). If A0 and A3 shared a block with A0 first, A3 would never execute and the pre-fix run would short-circuit on the missing index -- resurrecting the precise failure §7.1 opens by rejecting, and destroying the fail-first proof. A3 must not be preceded by A0 in the same block. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR raised this as MINOR M1, ELIXIR-DEV confirmed §7's flat-bullet wording permits the bad reading, and REVIEWER concurred.

=== THE FAIL-FIRST DEMONSTRATION IS MANDATORY, NOT OPTIONAL ===

§7.1 is explicit that this obligation must be PERFORMED, not declared satisfied. Run its procedure in a THROWAWAY GIT WORKTREE against pre-fix commit 3d19e8c -- never a `git checkout` in this checkout, which holds local main and has a live sibling worktree; CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR verified the worktree approach disturbs neither. Quote all four required outputs from §7.1 VERBATIM, no paraphrase, and state plainly that A0 is expected to fail in that same pre-fix run for the same reason so no reader is misled by two red assertions. Clean up the throwaway worktree when done.

The property that must be demonstrated: A3 fails pre-fix ON SIZE (over: [:lines, :bytes], ~4,217 lines / ~260,644 bytes) via the {:no_index_fallback, "docs/status/requirement_status.yaml"} resolution -- NOT on a missing file -- and passes post-fix because the current volume resolves through the index to v2. If what you actually observe differs from that table in any way, report it; do not adjust the test until it produces the expected story.

=== SCOPE ===

Do NOT run the full suite -- TEST-RUNNER owns that at Step 4c, and REVIEWER noted the project gate is currently RED for pre-existing reasons unrelated to this branch (ISS-0109/ISS-0116 class). Running your own new test file, and the pre-fix worktree run, is required and expected. Do not touch docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, its volumes, the index, or any file under handoffs/ or test/reports/. handoffs/orchestrator.log has uncommitted ORCH edits -- leave it, stage by explicit path, never `git add -A`.

ONE THING REVIEWER ASKED BE PASSED ON: the moment you add these .exs files, this branch stops being a zero-code change, so REVIEWER's proof that the branch adds no failure main lacks EXPIRES. Do not restate that proof as though it still holds; TEST-RUNNER re-establishes the baseline independently at Step 4c.

=== REWORK ITERATION 1 (dispatched by ORCH 2026-08-21T07:45Z) -- APPLY THE GATED §13 AMENDMENT ===

THIS IS NOT A CRITICISM OF YOUR STEP 4 WORK. Your PARTIAL was the correct verdict and your refusal to weaken A4 to clear its red is the reason this amendment exists at all. Everything you built stands: the fail-first demonstration, the §8 erratum, the one-block-per-assertion structure, the digest confirmation. What changed is that the design now has a mechanism for what A4 found.

WHAT HAPPENED SINCE. Your A4 red drove a design amendment (§13) which has now cleared CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's hard gate on re-gate pass 2, after the gate FAILed the first version on a real hole (a declared record could cite the CURRENT volume, making the exception list a declare-to-silence mechanism -- fixed by requiring every record's path: to name a `status: closed` volume carrying a `frozen_prefix_sha256:`). ELIXIR-DEV then applied §13.4's block to the index and §13.8's addendum to v2's header at commit 25440db, and independently re-verified all three records against the on-disk entries. Your own A4 failure message was a third independent confirmation that the declared set equals the on-disk set exactly and that A5's vocabulary set is unaffected -- it reported 'shape violations (3)' naming exactly 4803/4896/5050 and 'undeclared vocabulary violations (0)'.

YOUR TASK NOW -- implement §13.5, §13.6 and §13.7:
  1. SPLIT A4 into A4a (vocabulary -- unchanged in substance) and A4b (shape), per §13.5. A4b asserts EXACT SET EQUALITY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS between the shape violations found on disk and the index's `known_shape_anomalies:`, across EVERY volume, closed and current.
  2. IMPLEMENT THE CLOSED-AND-PINNED RULE, which is the gate's MAJOR-1 fix and the single most important line of this pass: A4b additionally asserts that every `known_shape_anomalies:` record's `path:` names a volume whose index `volumes:` entry has `status: closed` AND carries a `frozen_prefix_sha256:`. It fires INDEPENDENTLY of set equality and EVEN WHEN the cited violation genuinely exists on disk. A record citing the current volume, or a path that is not a volume in the index at all, FAILS. Do not fold this into the set-equality comparison -- it is a separate assertion with its own failure mode, and collapsing them would lose exactly the property the gate demanded.
  3. IMPLEMENT §13.5's SPECIFIED FAILURE OUTPUT. This is now part of the contract, not an implementer's choice, because §13.9's visibility claim depends on it: on any failure -- either direction of set equality, or the closed-volume rule -- name EVERY element of the symmetric difference, one per line, with path, entry_line, req and kind (and field/found_as where set), LABELLED BY SIDE ('on disk but not declared' / 'declared but not on disk'), plus every record that failed the closed-volume rule with the volume status that disqualified it. A count, or 'the sets differ', is explicitly declared insufficient.
  4. ADD §13.7's TWO SIGNATURE-ONLY ADDITIONS to test/support/status_history.ex: `parse_index/1`'s return map gains `known_shape_anomalies:`, and a new `shape_anomalies(volume_path)`. `anomalies/3` is unchanged. Keep the module path-parameterised -- nothing may hardcode the index location.
  5. ADD A8 CLAUSE (c): the current volume's header must contain the literal token `known_shape_anomalies:`, so a volume opened by copying the header cannot silently drop the declaration at roll time. ELIXIR-DEV confirmed the token is present on disk at v2:72.
  6. FOLD IN MINOR-5, a one-line design correction the gate raised on its final pass and which ORCH authorizes you to make in the artefact (same narrow authorization as §8's erratum, and no wider): §13.10 still says unconditionally to DECLARE a fourth shape violation, which is now WRONG for the current volume -- there, the only lawful action is to fix it in the working tree before committing, because a record citing an open volume fails A4b. §13.10 is the section an applying agent treats as authoritative, so correct it there. Change nothing else in the artefact.

VERIFY. Run the invariant file and quote the real result. A4a and A4b must both be GREEN once §13.4's records and the on-disk violations agree. Then prove A4b actually bites rather than merely passing -- exercise its two failure modes against temporary fixtures or an in-test path parameter (never by editing the real index or any volume): (i) a declared record that is not on disk, and (ii) a record citing an open, unpinned volume. Quote both failure messages, and confirm they carry the §13.5 content specified above. A4b that is green because it asserts nothing would be the worst possible outcome of this entire run.

DO NOT: edit docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (frozen, zero bytes -- and the digest must stay 5a1a64ab...804), edit the real index or v2 to make a test pass, delete or alter any of the three declared records, or narrow the detector. §13.10's rule stands: a fourth violation is never suppressed by deleting a record or weakening the check.

BASELINE, unchanged from your last brief: REVIEWER's Step 3d no-added-failure proof has expired and must not be restated. ELIXIR-DEV observed 13 failures at 25440db (9 Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest, 2 Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest, 1 your A4) without re-deriving a main baseline. Do not run the full suite -- TEST-RUNNER owns that and the baseline at Step 4c.

C1: the corrected digest form (trim "\n" then "\r", never the two-byte "\r\n") computes 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804 on this CRLF working tree -- EQUAL to the normative Bash value and to the index's frozen_prefix_sha256; §8 CHECK 5 is now discharged (A6 green). A0 failed in the same run for exactly that reason and the spec says so plainly. Post-fix, the same unmodified file gives 9/10 passed with A3 and A0 both green. Worktree removed and verified gone. Both are detailed below and in test/specs/ISS-0119.md §6 and §4. || REWORK ITERATION 1 (2026-08-21T07:54:09Z), applying the gated §13 amendment. §13.5/§13.6/§13.7 are implemented and the file is GREEN: `mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs` -> `Result: 13 passed` (A0, A1, A2, A3, A3b, A4a, A4b, A4b-NC1, A4b-NC2, A5, A6, A7, A8), zero compile warnings, `mix format --check-formatted` clean. A4 IS SPLIT: A4a is the vocabulary limb (unchanged in substance, GREEN); A4b is the shape limb, asserting exact set equality in BOTH directions over the identity key {path, entry_line, kind, field, found_as} against the index's `known_shape_anomalies:`, across every volume. Its on-disk set is EXACTLY the three records ELIXIR-DEV declared at 25440db -- no fourth shape violation exists, stated explicitly because §13.10 requires it be stated either way. THE CLOSED-AND-PINNED RULE IS A SEPARATE ASSERTION, NOT PART OF THE SET COMPARISON. `a4b_findings/1` computes `not_closed_and_pinned` independently of `undeclared`/`unfound`; the single combined assert exists only so that no limb can mask another by ExUnit's first-failure abort. A record whose `path:` names a volume that is not `status: closed` with a `frozen_prefix_sha256:` -- including a path that is not a volume at all -- fails even when the violation it cites genuinely exists on disk. A4b BITES, PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. Two negative-control blocks drive the SAME `a4b_findings/1` the A4b block asserts on, against throwaway fixtures under the system tmp dir removed by `on_exit` -- the real index and the real volumes were never touched. (i) declared-but-not-on-disk yields `declared but not on disk (1) ... path=<tmp>/v1.yaml  entry_line=3  req="REQ-001"  kind="missing_field"  field="note"`. (ii) THE ONE THE GATE DEMANDED: the fixture's CURRENT volume genuinely lacks `note:` and the record matches it exactly, so set equality is GREEN (`on disk but not declared (0)` / `declared but not on disk (0)`) and A4b still goes RED with `records citing a volume that is not closed-and-pinned (1): path=<tmp>/v2.yaml  entry_line=3  req="REQ-002"  kind="missing_field"  field="note"  -> volume status: "current" (must be "closed")`. 0/0 with a red verdict is the property in one line. Both messages are quoted in full in test/specs/ISS-0119.md §6.3 and both carry §13.5's specified content: every element of the symmetric difference named one per line with path/entry_line/req/kind (plus field/found_as where set), labelled by side, plus every disqualified record with the volume status that disqualified it -- a count alone is explicitly insufficient. §13.7's two signature-only additions are in test/support/status_history.ex: `parse_index/1`'s map gains `known_shape_anomalies:` (with the index's literal `null` normalised to `nil` so a declaration compares equal to a detection), and a new `shape_anomalies/1` detector emitting missing_field | misnamed_field | extra_field | field_order, with a misnamed field counted as ONE violation and never also as a missing_field. `anomalies/3` is UNCHANGED and still reports vocabulary only, so A5 is arithmetically unaffected (§13.6) and stayed green. issues.description: RESOLVED, recorded rather than dropped: the Step 4 MAJOR (A4 red on three undeclared shape anomalies in frozen volume 1) is closed. It was NOT closed by weakening the test. CODE-DESIGNER's §13 gave it a mechanism (`known_shape_anomalies:`), CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR failed §13's first version on a declare-to-silence hole and passed it on re-gate pass 2 once the closed-and-pinned rule was added, ELIXIR-DEV applied the index block and the v2 header addendum at 25440db, and this pass implemented §13.5-§13.7. The three volume-1 entries (4803 REQ-053 missing note, 4896 REQ-056 timestamp-for-at, 5050 REQ-054 missing note) are DECLARED, not corrected: volume 1 is byte-identical and A6 still hashes to 5a1a64ab...804. The full first-run failure output is kept verbatim in test/specs/ISS-0119.md §6.1 as the record.

DESIGN CORRECTION MADE UNDER MINOR-5 (ORCH-authorized, narrow). §13.10 instructed an applying agent to DECLARE a fourth shape violation unconditionally. That contradicts the closed-and-pinned rule §13.5 gained on re-amendment iteration 1: a record citing the current volume fails A4b, so in the current volume the only lawful action is to fix the entry in the working tree before the commit lands. §13.10 now splits the response by volume status and carries a dated marker saying what was corrected and why. This was the only edit to the artefact in this pass.

A4b is ONE ExUnit block containing ONE assert over five independently-computed lists (undeclared, unfound, not_closed_and_pinned, misattributed, unparseable_at), not five asserts. This is deliberate and is the opposite of collapsing the rules: separate asserts would let ExUnit's first-failure abort hide the closed-and-pinned result behind a set-equality failure, which is exactly the masking §13.5 forbids by specifying that the message report both. C3 (one block per assertion) is satisfied -- A4a and A4b are the two assertions §13.5 defines, and each has its own block.

TWO NEGATIVE-CONTROL TEST BLOCKS were added beyond A0-A8 (A4b-NC1, A4b-NC2). They are not acceptance criteria; they exist because a green A4b that asserts nothing would be the worst outcome of this run, and they are the standing proof that both of its failure modes fire. They use throwaway tmp-dir fixtures removed by on_exit, no wall-clock time and no unseeded randomness, and they never read or write docs/status/. TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should treat them as coverage of the detector, not of the requirement.

REVIEWER's Step 3d proof that this branch adds no failure main lacks REMAINS EXPIRED and is not restated. ELIXIR-DEV observed 13 failures at 25440db (9 Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest, 2 Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest, 1 A4) without re-deriving a main baseline; the A4 one is now green. The full suite was not run here. TEST-RUNNER must re-establish the baseline independently at Step 4c.
